_note: Thai administrative, registry and trade vocabulary, glossed by hand. These are DICTIONARY WORDS AND ADMINISTRATIVE TERMS, never a place's name: nothing here is a candidate for nameEn, and nothing here is machine translated. A gloss says what the word means; the reading beside it (translit.py, RTGS) says how it sounds. Read by terms.py, folded into data/trade_lexicon.json by importers/build_trade_lexicon.py, and printed as `.en` beside the Thai so the language toggle can reach it.
_why: Nan, 2026-09-06 and again 2026-09-08 with Michael: terms that exist in only one script shut out every reader who does not have that script, and hide the patterns a reader could otherwise infer. Measured 2026-09-08: 33,369 Thai-only values printed on the pages across 59 attribute fields, with the FIELD LABELS bilingual and the VALUES Thai alone.

parts._note: Words that compose. A value is glossed by glossing its parts, so a combination nobody has seen yet still reads. Order inside a field is preserved.

levels._numbered_note: ป.1–ป.6 are Grades 1–6 and ม.1–ม.6 are Grades 7–12, which is the offset. A parent reading in English wants the grade, not the Thai stage's number.

prefix._note: The one-letter address prefixes. Printed in front of a name, they are the difference between a road and a district and half the tambon of Chiang Mai are also road names.

separators._note: Kept as they are, so a glossed value has the shape of the Thai one.

agency._note: The 13 Thai agency names the records credit as their source, each under the English name the agency itself publishes. A credit line that only a Thai reader can read tells an English reader nothing about how much to trust the row. Whole-string match, never composed — an agency's name is its name.
